name: previous-next-links
title: Previous and next links
summary: Offers the page before and the page after the one a person is on, in a sequence of pages: two links, each named by a direction and the title of where it leads.

anatomy.description: The navigation landmark: one row with a place for the previous item at its start and a place for the next item at its end. It draws nothing of its own.
An item's shape: the whole of it is one link. It has no fill at rest and is where hover, focus and press are drawn.
An item's edge: the one hairline, which bounds what is pressed.

The arrow the previous and next links draw in an item: arrow_back at the start edge of the previous item, arrow_forward at the end edge of the next. Decorative; mirrored in a right-to-left layout by the icon helper.
The direction in a word of the product's ("Previous", "Next"), above the title.
The title of the page the item leads to. It wraps and is never cut.
The indicator shown for keyboard focus, around an item's container.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the landmark ("Pages", "Chapter navigation"), in the product's language. Tanrei ships no words of its own. It tells this landmark from the page's other navigation, so it is required.

items.name: item
items.summary: One neighbouring page of the sequence: a link to it, named by a direction and its title.

props.name: direction
props.description: Which neighbour the item leads to. previous: the page before, placed at the start with the arrow arrow_back. next: the page after, placed at the end with the arrow arrow_forward. A pair of previous and next links holds at most one item of each.

props.name: label
props.description: The direction in the product's words ("Previous", "Next"; "Newer", "Older"). It is drawn above the title and begins the item's accessible name.

props.name: title
props.description: The title of the page the item leads to ("Installation"). Empty, the item shows its direction alone (PNL-7).

props.name: href
props.description: The destination: an address as the platform's links take one. Empty, there is no page on that side and the item is not drawn (PNL-3), so a product can always give both items and leave one without a destination on the first and the last page.

events.name: click
events.description: The item was activated by pointer, touch, Enter or assistive technology. It is emitted before the destination opens; a product that takes the navigation itself (a client-side router) cancels it (PNL-14).

behavior.text: THE previous and next links SHALL be one navigation landmark named by label that holds its items in reading order — the previous item, then the next item, whatever order the product gave them in — and nothing else; WHILE label is empty THE previous and next links SHALL still render, and in debug builds report that the landmark has no accessible name.
behavior.verify: On the web: a nav element with the accessible name of label; the previous anchor precedes the next anchor in the document and in the focus order, in both layout directions.

behavior.text: WHILE an item's href is a destination THE previous and next links SHALL draw that item as the platform's own link to it (the web's anchor element in the document itself, not in a shadow root; SwiftUI's Link; on Compose, Flutter and React Native an element with the platform's link semantics whose address is opened by the platform's opener), so that whatever the platform gives a link — on the web its context menu, opening in a new tab or window, copying and dragging its address, the address shown before it is followed, a crawler that reads it, and a link that works before any script has run — is the platform's, and not the previous and next links's to draw or to take over; it SHALL expose the link role, named by the item's label followed by its title, with the arrow hidden from assistive technology, and WHERE the platform's links can say how a destination relates to the page (the web's rel) SHALL say previous for the previous item and next for the next.
behavior.verify: On the web, with scripting turned off: two a elements with their href, rel prev and rel next; the accessible name of the fixture both's next item is "Next Design tokens".

behavior.text: IF an item's href is empty or only white space THE previous and next links SHALL draw nothing for that item and expose nothing for it, because the sequence has no page on that side; IF it names a script to run rather than a place to go (the web's javascript: scheme) or cannot be read as an address by the platform, or direction names a value the previous and next links do not have, or a second item has the direction of an earlier one, THE previous and next links SHALL likewise draw nothing for that item and in debug builds report it. WHILE no item has a destination THE previous and next links SHALL draw nothing, take no room and expose no landmark.
behavior.verify: The fixture next-only holds a previous item with an empty href: one link is exposed and one is drawn.

behavior.text: THE previous and next links SHALL lay its row out in two columns of equal width, comp.previous-next-links.gap apart, with the previous item in the column at the start and the next item in the column at the end, each as wide as its column and both as high as the taller of the two; an item that is not drawn SHALL leave its column empty, so that the next item stands at the same place and has the same width on every page of the sequence.
behavior.verify: The fixtures both and next-only draw their next item at the same place and width.

behavior.text: WHERE the layout gives the previous and next links less width than two times comp.previous-next-links.container.min-width plus comp.previous-next-links.gap THE previous and next links SHALL stack its items instead: each drawn item as wide as the previous and next links, the previous item above the next, comp.previous-next-links.gap between them, and no room kept for an item that is not drawn. It SHALL decide this by the width it is given, not by the window's.
behavior.verify: Under the default system the items stack below a width of 496. Test by setting the width of the stage; a fixture cannot.

behavior.text: THE previous and next links SHALL draw each item as a container with corners comp.previous-next-links.container.shape and an edge comp.previous-next-links.outline.width wide inside it, its content comp.previous-next-links.container.padding from the edge on every side: the arrow in a box comp.previous-next-links.icon.size large — arrow_back at the start edge of the previous item, arrow_forward at the end edge of the next — centred on the item's height, comp.previous-next-links.container.gap from the text, and the text filling the rest of the width, its lines aligned to the start in the previous item and to the end in the next, so that each item's text stands beside its arrow.
behavior.verify: Under the default system: corners 8, an edge of 1, 16 of padding, a 20 arrow 12 from the text.

behavior.text: THE previous and next links SHALL set an item's label in comp.previous-next-links.label.typescale and, comp.previous-next-links.label.gap under it, its title in comp.previous-next-links.title.typescale; it SHALL wrap both where their language allows a break and, for a run with no such place that is longer than the line, inside the run, and SHALL NOT cut them, draw an ellipsis or scroll. WHILE an item's title is empty THE previous and next links SHALL draw its label alone, in the title's text style and color. WHILE an item's label is empty THE previous and next links SHALL draw its title alone and in debug builds report that the item does not say its direction in words.
behavior.verify: The fixture long-titles wraps both titles on the stage; nothing is hidden and both items have the height of the taller. The fixture labels-only draws "Newer" and "Older" in the title's style.

behavior.text: WHILE an item is hovered, keyboard-focused or pressed THE previous and next links SHALL render its container, outline, label, title, arrow and opacity from the component tokens of the highest-precedence active state, with precedence pressed over focused over hovered (comp.previous-next-links.item.container.color, comp.previous-next-links.item.outline.color, comp.previous-next-links.item.label.color, comp.previous-next-links.item.title.color and comp.previous-next-links.item.icon.color at rest); focus gained by pointer or touch SHALL NOT select the focused state.

WHEN an item receives keyboard focus THE previous and next links SHALL show the focus ring around that item's container without animation — the system's focus indicator, sys.focus.offset from the container, sys.focus.outer-width wide in the focus-ring color, with the inner stroke of sys.focus.inner-width where the system has one; focus gained by pointer or touch SHALL NOT show it.

WHEN an item is pressed by pointer, touch or Enter THE previous and next links SHALL show the pressed state without delay and SHALL keep it visible for at least sys.motion.duration.press-hold, even when the press ends sooner.

WHILE pressed THE previous and next links SHALL answer as sys.behavior.pressed-feedback names: overlay applies the pressed tokens to the whole container at once; ripple grows the pressed state layer from the point of contact (from the center for keyboard activation); dim applies the pressed opacity to the whole control and draws no state layer; none draws no answer to the press. Under ripple and dim only the container color stays with the state under the press; label, title, icon, outline, opacity and shape still come from the pressed tokens. Under none every part stays with the state under the press. The ripple grows over comp.previous-next-links.motion.feedback-duration with motion.state-easing, fades over motion.state-duration with motion.state-easing once the press has ended and press-hold has passed, and appears whole where motion is reduced.
behavior.verify: Test under a system that sets each value; `m3-like` is ripple, `cupertino` is dim, the default is overlay. The control is the pressed item, never both.

behavior.text: THE previous and next links SHALL ease its container corners by sys.shape.corner-smoothing (0 is a quarter circle, 0.6 the iOS continuous corner; a platform with only the OS curve draws it for any amount above 0) and show its keyboard focus as sys.behavior.focus-style names (ring or glow); a platform that cannot draw a choice SHALL fall back to the first value and state that in its README.
behavior.verify: `cupertino` is continuous; the `acme` fixture system is glow.

behavior.text: THE previous and next links SHALL change an item between its states over comp.previous-next-links.motion.state-duration with comp.previous-next-links.motion.state-easing, and at once where motion is reduced.

WHEN the user activates an item by pointer, touch or Enter THE previous and next links SHALL emit that item's click exactly once and then open its href where the person is, unless the product cancelled that click, in which case it SHALL open nothing: the product's own router has taken the navigation. It SHALL NOT hold the navigation back for sys.motion.duration.press-hold. THE previous and next links SHALL NOT activate an item on Space, which on the web scrolls the page as it does on any link, and SHALL NOT show the pressed state for it; WHERE the platform gives its links other keys or gestures (on the web a modified or a middle click that opens a new tab, on Apple platforms a long press that previews) THE previous and next links SHALL leave them to the platform.
behavior.verify: On the web: Enter follows the link and fires click once; Space fires no click and leaves the page to scroll; a click listener that calls preventDefault() keeps the page where it is.

behavior.text: WHERE the visual size of an item is below the minimum target THE previous and next links SHALL extend its hit area on both axes to sys.target.touch for touch input and sys.target.pointer for fine pointers, without changing its visual size; a platform that cannot tell the input type SHALL use sys.target.touch.
behavior.verify: Under the default system an item is 76 high or more (16 of padding, a 16 label line, 2, a 26 title line, 16 of padding), so nothing is extended; a layer with less padding is where this is seen.

behavior.text: THE previous and next links SHALL open a destination in the context the person is in and in no other, SHALL draw no mark for a new context and SHALL draw no state for a destination already visited: the pages of one sequence replace one another, and an item's colors say what it is and what state it is in.

THE previous and next links SHALL draw each arrow through the platform's icon helper, as a glyph of the system's icon set, in the icon color of its state, with sys.icon.family.unselected and sys.icon.fill.unselected, sys.icon.weight and an optical size clamped between sys.icon.optical-size.min and sys.icon.optical-size.max; it SHALL take no glyph from the product and SHALL draw no path of its own.

WHERE the platform draws with a person's own forced colors (the web's forced-colors mode, and a platform's equivalent where it has one) THE previous and next links SHALL draw each item's edge, label, title and arrow in the platform's link color, keeping the edge comp.previous-next-links.outline.width wide so that what is pressed stays bounded, and SHALL draw the focus ring in the platform's highlight color.
behavior.verify: On the web, with forced colors emulated: the text and the border are LinkText.

behavior.text: WHILE the text size is enlarged THE previous and next links SHALL grow each item with its text — both items of a row to the height of the taller — keeping comp.previous-next-links.container.padding, comp.previous-next-links.container.gap, comp.previous-next-links.label.gap, comp.previous-next-links.gap and the arrow at comp.previous-next-links.icon.size, and SHALL still stack by the width it is given (PNL-5).
behavior.verify: At 200 % text size no text is cut or overlaps, and the page does not scroll sideways.

behavior.text: THE previous and next links SHALL take its layout direction from where it is used — the direction of the nearest ancestor that sets one, and the platform's own where none does — and SHALL have no direction setting of its own; WHEN that direction changes while the previous and next links are shown THE previous and next links SHALL draw itself for the new direction at once, without a motion of its own, keeping its focus.
behavior.verify: Test with the direction set on an ancestor inside the page or the view tree, not on the root, and again changed after the first render.

behavior.text: WHERE the layout direction is right-to-left THE previous and next links SHALL mirror its row and each item's content by logical start and end, so that the previous item stands at the right with its arrow at its right edge and the next item at the left with its arrow at its left edge, and SHALL draw both arrows mirrored left to right, so that the previous item's points to the right and the next item's to the left: the icon helper mirrors them inside their own boxes because the system's icon set marks arrow_back and arrow_forward as mirrored. THE previous and next links SHALL NOT mirror a glyph itself, and the reading and focus order SHALL stay previous, then next.
behavior.verify: The fixture both-rtl: «السابق» at the right with an arrow pointing right, «التالي» at the left with an arrow pointing left. A system whose icon set marks neither name draws them unmirrored.

behavior.text: THE previous and next links SHALL lay out each label and each title as text of its own direction, isolated from the text around it: it takes the base direction of its first strong character, or the layout direction where it has none, so that a left-to-right name, a number with its sign or unit and a version keep their own order in a right-to-left layout and reorder nothing beside them; THE previous and next links SHALL still place the text and align its lines by the layout direction and the item's side (PNL-6), not by the text's own.
behavior.verify: The fixture ltr-title-rtl draws a left-to-right title in a right-to-left stage: the title reads in its own order and its lines are aligned as the Arabic label above it.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the previous item, then to the next: each drawn item is a tab stop, as the links of a navigation region are.
Follows the focused item. Space does what it does on any link (on the web it scrolls the page).

accessibility.labeling: The landmark is named by label, which is required: a page has other navigation, and the name tells this one apart. Each item is a link named by its label and then its title ("Next Design tokens"), both of which are drawn, so the name a person hears holds the words a person sees; the arrow is decorative. Nothing is added to the name.
notes: An item is a link and never a button: it has a destination, and without one it is not drawn. Paging by number — the pages of a list or a result set, with or without an address for each — is Pagination, a component of its own: these links say where they lead by its title, a page number says nothing of the sort.

An item is pressed as a whole, so its title is not a second link and is not underlined. A text link is underlined because nothing else tells it from the text beside it; an item is told by its edge, its arrow and its place, none of which is a color. In forced colors the edge and the text take the platform's link color (PNL-18).
The reading and focus order is previous, then next, in both layout directions and when the items stack; the visual order follows it (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3).
The direction is said in words by label. The arrow repeats it for sighted people and is hidden from assistive technology; an item with an empty label is reported in debug builds.
The next item keeps its place when there is no previous page (PNL-4): a person who pages through a sequence finds it where it was.
Text must remain readable at 200% text size: titles wrap and are never cut, the items grow, and the row stacks by the width it has (PNL-5, PNL-19).

Contrast in the default system: the title is on-surface and the label and the arrow on-surface-variant, both held to 4.5:1 (7:1 in the high-contrast schemes) on every surface by the token invariants. The edge is outline-variant, the one hairline: it is not held to 3:1, and it does not need to be, because the label, the title and the arrow identify the item without it (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of what is required to identify a control). The focus ring is held to 3:1 against every surface.

How a state looks is a value decision of the active design system (a state-layer mix in Tanrei, a dim or no hover at all elsewhere). The previous and next links read the state's tokens and never computes the effect itself.
A pair of previous and next links belongs after the content it pages, once per page. A product that prints its pages hides it in print.

web.name: tanrei-previous-next-links

item.name: tanrei-previous-next-links-item
item.notes: A class on the product's own anchor. `data-direction` is `previous` or `next`; the anchor also carries `rel="prev"` or `rel="next"`. The label and the title are two spans with their classes, in that order.

web.notes:
Classes on the product's own elements, as Link is: `
PreviousInstallation…
`, styled by a stylesheet of the package. The anchors are in the document, so they are links before any script runs and for whatever reads the page as built (PNL-2). The stylesheet alone gives the whole component: the two columns are a grid in which each item takes the column of its `data-direction`, whatever its place in the markup, and an anchor without `href` is not displayed (PNL-3); stacking is a container query on the nav (PNL-5); the arrows are the items' `::before` and `::after` in the icon font, mirrored under `:dir(rtl)`; the states and the press-hold are the stylesheet's as they are Link's. The package's script, where it is loaded, adds through its one listener on the document what a stylesheet cannot: the shared press primitive (ripple and dim, PNL-11), the reordering of items given next-first so that the focus order is right, and every debug report. The web is not a custom element here, so `packages/tools/src/conventions.js` needs an entry for where the implementation lives, as prose has. React: `PreviousNextLinks` renders the same markup and takes a `render` prop for a router's link.

swiftui.name: TanreiPreviousNextLinks

item.name: TanreiPreviousNextLinksItem
item.notes: `TanreiPreviousNextLinksItem(.next, label: "Next", title: "Design tokens", destination: url, action:)`; `destination` is an optional `URL`, and `nil` is the empty href.

swiftui.notes: `TanreiPreviousNextLinks(label:previous:next:)`, each item optional. Each item is built on SwiftUI's `Link`; `action` runs before the address opens and returns whether the link should still open it (the environment's `OpenURLAction` does the opening). The container has the navigation landmark through an accessibility container with `label`. The row stacks with `ViewThatFits` measured against the proposed width.

compose.name: TanreiPreviousNextLinks

item.name: TanreiPreviousNextLinksItem
item.notes: A data class; `href` is nullable. `onClick` returns false to keep the address closed; otherwise `LocalUriHandler.current` opens it.

compose.notes: `TanreiPreviousNextLinks(previous, next, contentDescription, modifier)`. Compose has no navigation landmark and no link role for a clickable element: the row is a semantics group named by `contentDescription`, and its README says what is not exposed. Stacking reads the incoming constraints (`BoxWithConstraints`).

flutter.name: TanreiPreviousNextLinks

item.name: TanreiPreviousNextLinksItem
item.notes: A value class; `href` is nullable. `onPressed` returns false to keep the address closed; otherwise the opener the app provides opens it.

flutter.notes: `TanreiPreviousNextLinks(previous: …, next: …, semanticLabel: …)`. `Semantics(container: true, label:)` around the row; each item `Semantics(link: true)`, with `linkUrl` where the engine has it. Stacking reads the incoming constraints (`LayoutBuilder`).

react-native.name: PreviousNextLinks

item.name: PreviousNextLinksItem
item.notes: An object of the `previous` or the `next` prop. `onPress` receives an event whose `preventDefault()` keeps the address closed; otherwise `Linking.openURL(href)`.

react-native.notes: `<PreviousNextLinks accessibilityLabel="Pages" previous={{ label, title, href }} next={…} />`. Each item is a `Pressable` with `accessibilityRole="link"`; the row has `accessibilityRole="navigation"` where the platform maps it (the web target) and is a labelled group elsewhere. Stacking reads `onLayout`. Follows the app's direction where an ancestor's is not known.
